chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, and Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, altogether from Ibn Mahboub, from Jameel ibn Salih, from Al-Fuzayl ibn Yasaar, who said:
I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about an owned man who pronounced Zahaar from his wife, so he (peace be upon him) said to me: 'Zahaar does not occur, nor Ila', until he copulates with her.'

key_terms.إِيلَاء: Ila: An oath by a husband to abstain from sexual intercourse with his wife for four months or more.
key_terms.ظِهَار: Zahaar: A form of divorce in pre-Islamic and early Islamic law where a husband declares his wife to be like his mother's back, making intercourse forbidden until expiation.
key_terms.مُمْلَكٍ: Mamlak: An owned slave or servant.
key_terms.يُدْخَلَ بِهَا: Yudkhala biha: He enters/copulates with her (consummation of marriage).

ai.seo_question: What is the condition for Zahaar to be valid in Shia fiqh?
ai.summary: This hadith, narrated through the chain of Jamil ibn Salih and al-Fudayl ibn Yasar, establishes a critical prerequisite in Shia fiqh: Zahaar and Ila are legally ineffective until marital consummation (Dukhul) has occurred. This condition distinguishes these specific forms of marital separation from general divorce (Talaq), ensuring that the husband's oath or declaration carries weight only after the wife has become fully his in the legal and physical sense, a nuance deeply rooted in the interpretation of Surah Al-Mujadila.
